lesson.title: Git Interactive Rebase: Edit, Split, Squash, Delete, and Reorder Commits

sources.title: Git Interactive Rebase: Edit, Split, Squash, Delete, and Reorder Commits

steps.title: Set up repo and check branches
steps.instructions: In an empty folder, run git init -b main, commit index.js on main, then create feature/login with four commits (README.md, login endpoint with debug log, logout endpoint, cleanup, empty middleware commit). Run git branch -a to confirm feature/login has no remote branch.

targets.caption: Verify the feature branch is local and not pushed

explanations.topic: Never rebase commits that have already been pushed
Using git branch -a to check for remote branches

hints: Make sure you are in a fresh folder before running git init.
Create the base commit on main first, then branch off with git checkout -b feature/login.
Run git branch -a and verify there is no remotes/origin/feature/login entry.
common_mistakes: Rebasing a branch that has already been pushed to a shared remote.
Forgetting to create the four commits on feature/login before starting HEAD~4.
steps.code: git init -b main && printf "const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const port = 3000; const DEFAULT_USER = 'admin'; app.use(express.json()); app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.send('OK')); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Welcome to the Login App')); app.listen(port, () => console.log('Listening'));" > index.js && git add index.js && git commit -m "Add route for welcome message" && git checkout -b feature/login && printf "# Interactive Rebase Example" > README.md && printf "const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const port = 3000; const DEFAULT_USER = 'admin'; app.use(express.json()); app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.send('OK')); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Welcome to the Login App')); app.post('/login', (req, res) => { console.log('DEBUG: LOGIN REQUEST RECEIVED'); // Debugging block res.send('Login'); }); app.listen(port, () => console.log('Listening'));" > index.js && git add README.md index.js && git commit -m "Add README and login endpoint" && printf "const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const port = 3000; const DEFAULT_USER = 'admin'; app.use(express.json()); app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.send('OK')); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Welcome to the Login App')); app.post('/login', (req, res) => { res.send('Login'); }); app.post('/logout', (req, res) => { console.log('DEBUG: LOGOUT REQUEST RECEIVED'); res.send('Logout successful'); }); app.listen(port, () => console.log('Listening'));" > index.js && git add index.js && git commit -m "Add logout endpoint" && printf "const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const port = 3000; const DEFAULT_USER = 'admin'; app.use(express.json()); app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.send('OK')); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Welcome to the Login App')); app.post('/login', (req, res) => { res.send('Login'); }); app.post('/logout', (req, res) => { res.send('Logout successful'); }); app.listen(port, () => console.log('Listening'));" > index.js && git add index.js && git commit -m "Minor cleanup for logout route" && git commit --allow-empty -m "Add authentication middleware"

steps.title: Configure VS Code as Git editor
steps.instructions: Run git config --global core.editor "code --wait" so Git opens VS Code. Then run git rebase --interactive HEAD~4 on feature/login to open the commit list.

targets.caption: Configure VS Code as Git's editor

explanations.topic: How HEAD~4 or an ancestor hash selects commits to rebase
Why rebase opens Vim by default and how to exit with :q!

hints: If Vim opened earlier, press Escape and type :q! then Enter to abort without changes.
Run git config --global core.editor "code --wait" before starting the interactive rebase.
Run git rebase --interactive HEAD~4 and wait for git-rebase-todo to appear in VS Code.
common_mistakes: Omitting --wait in core.editor, causing Git to finish immediately before you edit the todo file.
Running HEAD~4 from main instead of checking out feature/login first.
steps.code: git checkout feature/login && git config --global core.editor "code --wait"

steps.title: Edit commit to remove debug code
steps.instructions: In git-rebase-todo, change pick to edit on the login endpoint commit, save and close the tab. Remove the debug console.log from index.js, run git add index.js, then git rebase --continue.

precision_checks.label: Debug logs removed from history
precision_checks.command: ! git log -p main..feature/login -- index.js | grep -q '^+.*DEBUG: LOGIN'

targets.caption: Replace pick with edit on the commit to modify
Stage the cleaned file and continue the rebase

explanations.topic: Why git-rebase-todo lists commits in reverse chronological order
What the default pick command does
Why editing a commit does not purge sensitive secrets from Git history

hints: Change only the first line's pick keyword to edit, then save and close git-rebase-todo.
When Git pauses, remove the debug print and commented lines from index.js and save the file.
Stage index.js with git add index.js, run git rebase --continue, and close COMMIT_EDITMSG.
common_mistakes: Saving git-rebase-todo without closing the editor tab, leaving Git waiting.
Forgetting to run git add index.js before running git rebase --continue.
steps.code: edit a7d22de Add README and login endpoint

steps.title: Split one commit into two commits
steps.instructions: Start git rebase --interactive HEAD~4, mark the README-and-login commit as edit, and close the todo file. Run git reset HEAD~1, commit README.md and index.js separately, then git rebase --continue.

precision_checks.label: Login commit exists
precision_checks.command: git log --oneline feature/login | grep -q 'Add login endpoint'

targets.caption: Undo the paused commit, keep changes

explanations.topic: Atomic commits and keeping unrelated changes separate
How git reset HEAD~1 moves committed changes back to working tree

hints: Pause at the first commit again using edit in git-rebase-todo.
Run git reset HEAD~1, then check git status to see README.md and index.js ready to be committed individually.
Create one commit for README.md and a second commit for index.js before running git rebase --continue.
common_mistakes: Using git reset --hard HEAD~1, which deletes the uncommitted changes instead of keeping them.
Running git commit --amend instead of making two separate commits after git reset HEAD~1.
steps.code: git reset HEAD~1 && git add README.md && git commit -m "Add README" && git add index.js && git commit -m "Add login endpoint"

steps.title: Squash, delete, and reorder commits
steps.instructions: Run git rebase --interactive HEAD~5 and change the cleanup commit from pick to squash, closing the todo and message editors. Then run git rebase --interactive HEAD~4, delete the middleware line, move the README commit below the logout commit, and close the file.

targets.caption: Squash the cleanup commit into the preceding logout commit
Move this line below the logout commit to reorder

explanations.topic: How squash merges a commit into the commit above it
Deleting commits by removing lines and reordering by moving lines

hints: Use HEAD~5 for the squash step because splitting the earlier commit left five commits on feature/login.
Change pick to squash on Minor cleanup for logout route, then save and close both git-rebase-todo and COMMIT_EDITMSG.
In the final git rebase --interactive HEAD~4 todo file, delete the Add authentication middleware line and move the Add README line to the bottom.
common_mistakes: Putting squash on the very first commit in git-rebase-todo, which has no previous commit to squash into.
Using HEAD~4 instead of HEAD~5 right after splitting a commit into two.
steps.code: pick 50ef5bb Add login endpoint; pick 28939ae Add logout endpoint; pick cacd72e Add README
